Ran it all: the buy flow end to end (6.5/15 review in 6.8s; payment LIZQTFXX7G…, audit note QBHFBE4GHO…, StudyBuddy receipt Y63L2MA2… all live), the on-page verifier (✓ Match), the refund path on-chain (the log now reads 12 paid, 3 refunded), and mirror parity (card bytes identical on vercel and sites.tab.bot, hash 4bf394cf90e5… matches the on-chain pin; demo.mp4 is 200 on both).

Scores as it stands: Algorand 9, x402 7, Innovation 7, India impact 6, Completeness 7.

Top 6, by score impact:

One independent buyer (x402, 7→8). "1 distinct buyer account(s)" is the most damning number on the page for an agentic-commerce entry; both agents are yours. Get a third party to run scripts/buy.mjs once (a friend's machine, their own wallet), or add a paste-your-mnemonic sandbox buy, so the stats line honestly says 2 buyers.

Price in TestNet USDC, not self-minted MMTC (x402 + Algorand, 7→8). Your README says one config value; ASA 10458941 exists. This was round 1's top objection and it still stands. A recognizable unit also makes the ₹5–10/review claim concrete instead of denominated in a token you minted.

Fix the tamper demo's dead end (Completeness, 7→8). Right after a successful buy and a ✓ Match verify on the same page, clicking "Try a tampered review" (item three of your own Try list) returns "Buy a review first (or open a verify link), then try this." Store the last purchase's tx + review JSON in page state and have #vtamper/#vany default to it. The underlying logic is fine: I recomputed the canonical hash of the VERIFY_LINK review and it reproduces the anchored b8a5a8d499…6497d0, and a +3 score changes it. It's pure wiring.

Publish the agent-vs-human table on 10 graded answers (Impact, 6→7+). Impact is currently unfalsifiable: no human marks, and the log shows 2/10 and 7.5/15 on similar answers, plus drift between runs (6.5/15 for me vs 7.5 in the verify link on the same default answer). Even one human-graded set turns narrative into evidence. You already have this task open; it's the cheapest impact lever you own.

Purge the Concordium leftovers on StudyBuddy (Completeness). Its page meta description still says "buys answer reviews from badge-verified agents over x402 on Concordium." The seller page links StudyBuddy; a judge opening the buyer sees the whole Algorand pitch contradicted in the page source. One line, redeploy.

Make the refund enforceable or stop calling it on-chain (Innovation/x402). Today the refund is MainsMarker choosing to send the asset back with a note; nothing on-chain obliges it, which undercuts an accountability pitch. Cheapest honest version: StudyBuddy's policy verifies the audit note appeared within T seconds and treats silence as a dispute; better, a tiny escrow released on audit-note presence.

Two smaller notes: settlement took 4.5s live vs the "~3 s" claim on the page (cosmetic), and the verify-link prefill didn't populate the form in my browser run, though I may have mangled the long link myself, so retest that one before trusting it as a bug.
